title: Unique generator-normalized finite scalar tensor chain map
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions and let $\iota:E\to L$ be a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-embedding. For $F=E,L$, fix its valuation ring $\mathcal O_F$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$, work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], small relative to the universe of module sheaves. Put $R_{F,W}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $F=E,L$, with the canonical quotient projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the compatible quotient coefficient maps induced by the embedding [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and hence $j_W:R_{E,W}\to R_{L,W}$. Let $S_W$ be ordinary, uncompleted change of rings $M\mapsto R_{L,W}\otimes_{R_{E,W}}M$, sheafified, applied termwise to cochain complexes with differential $1\otimes d$ [def-pur-change-of-rings-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $1\otimes x$ for the canonical sheafification-unit tensor section, not an assertion that arbitrary sections are globally pure [def-sfb-scalar-extension-pure-tensor-section]. Let $W$ be any scheme and $n\in\mathbf N$, indexing quotient exponent $n+1$. For $F=E,L$ and cochain complexes $P,Q$ of $R_{F,W}$-modules, put $P_{F,n+1}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^{n+1})_W\otimes_{R_{F,W}}P$ and
$$T^F_{W,n}(P,Q)=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi^F_{n+1}}\operatorname{Tot}^{\oplus}(P_{F,n+1}\otimes_{(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^{n+1})_W}Q_{F,n+1}),$$
with the sheafified tensor, direct-sum totalization, and differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ for $x$ of degree $p$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. There exists exactly one natural transformation of bifunctors
$$\beta_n:S_W\circ T^E_{W,n}\longrightarrow T^L_{W,n}\circ(S_W\times S_W)$$
whose components are $R_{L,W}$-linear chain maps and which for every $P,Q$, degrees $p,q$, object $U\in W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and sections $x\in P^p(U)$, $y\in Q^q(U)$ satisfies, in the $(p,q)$ summand of degree $p+q$,
$$\beta_n(P,Q)^{p+q}\bigl(1\otimes((1\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y))\bigr)=(1\otimes(1\otimes x))\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes y)).$$
Naturality is with respect to every pair of chain maps, without flatness, K-flatness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of $\ell$ on $W$.

source.note: Retained original parent proof step 2 (H1, 2026-10-26), as construction material for this unsplit statement, not a completed proof: For pullback at each finite quotient level, use the scalar tensor and inverse-image adjunction universal properties to define the map sending 1 tensor f*(1 tensor x) to f*(1 tensor (1 tensor x)). The balanced relations, restriction maps, and differentials commute with this formula. Pure tensors and the inverse-image adjunction force uniqueness and naturality. For tensor at each level, the balanced tensor universal property gives 1 tensor ((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) mapping to (1 tensor (1 tensor x)) tensor (1 tensor (1 tensor y)). The signed total differential commutes by bidegree, and the coproduct universal property gives the total chain map and its uniqueness. These are exactly the two pre-existing holes; no new comparison assertion is introduced.

proof.text: Take the normalized natural chain transformation constructed by lem-pur-integral-scalar-tensor-level-construction. Its functors and generator equation are literally those in the present statement.

For a second normalized transformation, use natural-transformation extensionality and degreewise chain-map extensionality. The scalar adjunction first reduces equality to maps from the finite tensor complex. The finite_tensor_ext lemma from the existing tensor-level-reduction module tests them on the (p,q) total-tensor summands with p+q equal to the chosen degree, and on the two reduction unit generators. The scalar adjunction unit formula identifies these values with the normalization of the two transformations. Their equality on every such generator proves equality of the chain maps. Thus the constructed transformation is unique.

lean.note: The existing theorem and its scalarTensorLevelNormalization predicate state exactly this finite quotient-level natural transformation: existence and uniqueness of a natural chain map between the E and L tensor-level functors, normalized on all degreewise sheafification-unit pure tensors. The surrounding section variables provide prime l, finite Q_l-extensions E and L, and the Q_l-embedding ι; W and n are explicit theorem parameters. The theorem imposes no flatness, boundedness, K-flatness, constructibility, or invertibility assumptions.
lean.statement:
theorem scalarTensorLevel_existsUnique (W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃! α : integralOperationsTensorLevel l E W n ⋙
        (integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι W).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⟶
      ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι W).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).prod
        ((integralOrdinaryScalar l E L ι W).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙
          integralOperationsTensorLevel l L W n,
      scalarTensorLevelNormalization l E L ι W n α
